senses.def: a very strong interest in or enthusiasm for something
examples: Cooking has always been her passion.
He spoke with real passion about protecting the environment.

senses.def: a very strong feeling, especially of love or anger
examples: Their love affair was full of passion.
The debate stirred up strong passions on both sides.

note: Pattern: a passion FOR something.

senses.def: having or showing very strong feelings or beliefs about something
examples: She is passionate about animal rights.
He gave a passionate speech in defense of free speech.

senses.def: showing strong romantic or sexual love
examples: They shared a passionate kiss at the airport.

note: Pattern: passionate ABOUT something.

senses.def: accepting what happens without trying to change it or react
examples: Students shouldn't be passive listeners; they should ask questions.
Watching TV is a fairly passive activity.

senses.def: (grammar) in which the subject receives the action of the verb
examples: "The window was broken" is a passive sentence.

senses.def: the passive form of a verb
examples: Try rewriting the sentence in the passive.

note: Opposite: active. "Passive-aggressive" = showing anger indirectly.

senses.def: an official document that shows your nationality and that you need to travel abroad
examples: Don't forget your passport when you go to the airport.
My passport expires next year, so I need to renew it.

senses.def: something that makes it possible to achieve something
examples: Many people see education as a passport to a better life.

senses.def: a secret set of letters or numbers you type to use a computer system or account
examples: I forgot my password and had to reset it.
Use a strong password with numbers and symbols.

senses.def: the time before now, or a person's earlier life
examples: In the past, people wrote letters instead of emails.
She doesn't like talking about her past.

senses.def: gone by in time, or recent
examples: Prices have doubled over the past ten years.

senses.def: later than a time, or on the far side of something
examples: It's ten past six.
The bank is just past the traffic lights.

senses.def: from one side of something to the other
examples: A bus drove past without stopping.

note: Don't confuse past (noun/preposition) with passed (verb): "We passed the school" vs "We walked past the school".

senses.def: a minister in charge of a Christian church, especially a Protestant one
examples: The pastor gave a moving sermon on Sunday morning.
She asked the pastor to perform the wedding ceremony.

senses.def: a small area of something that is different from what is around it
examples: Drive carefully; there are icy patches on the road.
The dog has a white patch over one eye.

senses.def: a piece of material used to cover a hole or protect something
examples: He sewed a patch on the knee of his jeans.
The company released a security patch for the software.

senses.def: a period of time, especially a difficult one
examples: Their marriage went through a rough patch last year.

senses.def: to cover a hole or repair something with a piece of material
examples: We patched the hole in the roof before the rain came.

note: "Patch things up" = become friends again after an argument.

senses.def: an official right to be the only person or company to make or sell an invention
examples: The company holds a patent on the new battery design.
She applied for a patent for her invention.

senses.def: to get a patent for an invention
examples: He patented a new type of solar panel.

senses.def: (formal) obvious, used about something bad
examples: That was a patent lie, and everyone knew it.

note: "Patently" = clearly, obviously ("patently false").

senses.def: a narrow way for walking, made by people walking or built on purpose
examples: We followed a path through the woods to the lake.
The garden path was covered in leaves.

senses.def: the direction something moves in, or a way of doing something or reaching a goal
examples: The storm destroyed everything in its path.
Medicine was not the right career path for him.

note: "Our paths crossed" = we met by chance.

senses.def: a path or track for walking
examples: A stone pathway leads to the front door.

senses.def: a way of reaching a goal, or a route along which something moves, for example in the body
examples: The program offers a pathway to citizenship for young immigrants.
Scientists studied the nerve pathways involved in pain.

senses.def: the ability to stay calm when waiting or dealing with problems or annoying people
examples: Teaching small children takes a lot of patience.
I'm starting to lose patience with this slow internet.

senses.def: (British) a card game for one player
examples: My grandmother played patience every evening.

note: The card game is called solitaire in American English. Patience sounds like patients (plural of patient).

senses.def: a person receiving medical treatment, especially in a hospital
examples: The doctor sees about thirty patients a day.
Patients must wait in the lobby until their name is called.

senses.def: able to wait or deal with problems calmly, without getting annoyed
examples: Please be patient; your order will be ready soon.
She's very patient with her younger brother.

senses.def: the act of going around an area to check that there is no trouble, or the group that does this
examples: Soldiers are on patrol along the border.
A police patrol stopped the car at midnight.

senses.def: to go around an area regularly to check that it is safe
examples: Security guards patrol the parking lot all night.

note: Doubles the l: patrolled, patrolling.

senses.def: a person who gives money and support to artists, writers or a cause
examples: The wealthy family were patrons of the arts for generations.
She is a patron of several children's charities.

senses.def: (formal) a customer of a store, restaurant or other business
examples: The restaurant is popular with local patrons.
Library patrons can borrow up to ten books.

note: Trap: patron does NOT mean boss (Turkish "patron" = boss). "Patronizing" = treating someone as if they were stupid.

senses.def: the regular way in which something happens or is done
examples: Doctors noticed a pattern in the patients' symptoms.
Stress can change your sleep patterns.

senses.def: a repeated design of lines, shapes or colors
examples: She wore a dress with a floral pattern.

senses.def: a design or shape used as a guide for making something, especially clothes
examples: She used a pattern from a magazine to sew the skirt.

note: Trap: Turkish "patron" (sewing) = pattern in English.

senses.def: a short time when someone stops speaking or doing something
examples: After a long pause, she finally answered the question.
There was a brief pause in the fighting.

senses.def: to stop talking or doing something for a short time before continuing
examples: He paused for a moment to catch his breath.
Can you pause the movie? I need to get a drink.

note: "Give someone pause" = make them stop and think carefully.

senses.def: to give someone money for work, goods or services
examples: Can I pay by credit card?
She paid $40 for the concert tickets.

senses.def: to bring an advantage or benefit
examples: It pays to compare prices before you buy a car.

senses.def: the money someone gets for doing regular work
examples: Nurses are asking for better pay and working conditions.

note: Irregular: pay – paid – paid. Pay FOR the item: "I paid for dinner" (not "I paid dinner").

senses.def: an amount of money paid, or the act of paying
examples: The monthly payment on the car is $350.
We accept payment by cash or card.

note: "Down payment" = the first part of the price you pay when buying something big like a house (peşinat).

senses.def: a situation or time when there is no war or fighting
examples: The two countries signed a peace agreement last year.
The UN sent troops to keep the peace.

senses.def: a state of calm and quiet
examples: I just want some peace and quiet after a long day.
Meditation helps her find inner peace.

note: Don't confuse with piece (a part of something); they sound the same. "Peace of mind" = içi rahat olma.

senses.def: not involving war or violence
examples: The protest was peaceful, and no one was arrested.
Both sides want a peaceful solution to the conflict.

senses.def: quiet and calm
examples: We spent a peaceful afternoon by the lake.

senses.def: the point when something is at its highest, best or most successful
examples: Traffic is at its peak between 7 and 9 a.m.
She was at the peak of her career when she retired.

senses.def: the pointed top of a mountain
examples: Snow covered the mountain peaks.

senses.def: to reach the highest point or level
examples: Sales peaked in December and then fell.

senses.def: used to describe the busiest or highest level
examples: Flights are more expensive during peak season.

note: Don't confuse with peek (a quick look) or pique (interest).

senses.def: a poor farmer with a small piece of land, especially in the past or in poorer countries
examples: In the Middle Ages, most peasants worked on land owned by nobles.
The novel describes the hard lives of Russian peasants.

note: Mostly historical. Used about a modern person, it is an insult meaning rude or uneducated.

senses.def: strange or unusual, sometimes in an unpleasant way
examples: There's a peculiar smell coming from the basement.
It's peculiar that nobody saw him leave.

senses.def: belonging only to a particular person, place or thing
examples: This style of cooking is peculiar to the region.

senses.def: a person of the same age, status or ability as another person
examples: Teenagers often care more about what their peers think than their parents.
She was respected by her peers in the scientific community.

senses.def: to look carefully at something, especially because it is hard to see
examples: He peered through the fog, trying to see the road.

note: "Peer pressure" = influence from people your age to behave like them (akran baskısı).

senses.def: a tool for writing or drawing with ink
examples: Can I borrow a pen to sign this form?
Please fill out the application in black pen.

senses.def: a small fenced area for keeping animals
examples: The sheep were kept in a pen near the barn.

note: "Pen name" = a name an author uses instead of their real name (takma ad).

senses.def: a punishment for breaking a law, rule or contract
examples: The penalty for late payment is a $25 fee.
Many states have abolished the death penalty.

senses.def: a punishment or advantage given in a sports game when a player breaks a rule
examples: The referee gave the home team a penalty in the final minute.

senses.def: a thin wooden tool with a gray or colored center, used for writing or drawing
examples: Use a pencil so you can erase your mistakes.
The kids drew pictures with colored pencils.

senses.def: to write something with a pencil, or to plan something that may change later
examples: Let's pencil in a meeting for next Tuesday.

note: "Pencil something in" = arrange it provisionally, knowing it may change.

senses.def: (British) a small coin and unit of money; there are 100 pence in a pound
examples: The chocolate bar cost 99 pence, so I got a penny in change.

senses.def: (American) a cent, a coin worth one hundredth of a dollar
examples: She found a penny on the sidewalk and picked it up for luck.
The jar was full of pennies and dimes.

note: British plural for amounts is pence (50 pence); for coins, pennies. "Worth every penny" = worth the price.

senses.def: money paid regularly to someone who has retired or cannot work
examples: He lives on a small pension from the city.
The company contributes to its employees' pension plans.

note: Trap: pension is not "pansiyon" (a guesthouse is a guesthouse or B&B). Americans often say "retirement plan" or "401(k)".

senses.def: men, women and children; more than one person
examples: How many people are coming to dinner?
Most people prefer to work from home at least one day a week.

senses.def: all the people of a country, or a particular nation or ethnic group
examples: The president promised to serve the American people.
The museum tells the history of the native peoples of Alaska.

note: People is plural: "People are..." (not "people is"). "Peoples" means different nations or ethnic groups.

senses.def: a hot-tasting powder made from dried berries, used to flavor food
examples: Season the soup with salt and pepper.
Could you pass the pepper, please?

senses.def: a hollow vegetable that is red, green or yellow, sometimes very hot
examples: Slice two red peppers and add them to the salad.

senses.def: for each
examples: The tickets cost $15 per person.
The speed limit is 65 miles per hour.

senses.def: (formal) according to
examples: As per your request, I've attached the invoice.

note: In everyday speech "a" is common instead: "$10 an hour", "three times a day". "Per capita" = per person.

senses.def: (British spelling) one part in every hundred
examples: Prices have risen by five per cent this year.
Only 20 per cent of the students passed.

senses.def: in or for every hundred
examples: I agree with you a hundred per cent.

note: British spelling. American English writes it as one word: percent.

senses.def: to understand or think of someone or something in a particular way
examples: Many people perceive the city as dangerous, but crime is actually low.
She was perceived as a strong leader.

senses.def: to notice or become aware of something
examples: Dogs can perceive sounds that humans cannot hear.

note: Spelling rule: "i before e except after c" – perceive, receive.

senses.def: one part in every hundred, written as %
examples: About 60 percent of Americans own their homes.
The store is offering 30 percent off all shoes.

senses.def: by or in every hundred
examples: Sales rose 12 percent compared with last year.
I'm not a hundred percent sure.

note: American spelling (British: per cent). Use a number before percent; without a number, use percentage: "a high percentage".

senses.def: an amount or rate expressed as a part of one hundred
examples: A large percentage of the population lives in cities.
What percentage of your salary do you save?

note: "A percentage point" is the difference between two percentages: from 4% to 6% is a rise of 2 percentage points.

senses.def: an idea or belief you have based on how something seems to you
examples: There is a public perception that crime is rising.
Social media can distort our perception of reality.

senses.def: the ability to notice or understand things through the senses
examples: Alcohol affects your perception of distance.

senses.def: having no mistakes or faults; as good as it can be
examples: Nobody's perfect; everyone makes mistakes.
The weather was perfect for a picnic.

senses.def: exactly right for a particular purpose or person
examples: This apartment is perfect for a young couple.

senses.def: to make something as good as it can be
examples: She spent years perfecting her recipe for apple pie.

note: Stress: adjective PERfect, verb perFECT /pərˈfekt/. "A perfect stranger" = someone you don't know at all.

senses.def: completely; used to emphasize something
examples: You know perfectly well what I mean.
It's perfectly normal to feel nervous before an exam.

senses.def: in a perfect way; very well
examples: The dress fits perfectly.

note: Very often used for emphasis, not literal perfection: "perfectly happy" = completely happy.

senses.def: to entertain an audience by acting, singing, dancing or playing music
examples: The band will perform live at the festival on Saturday.
The students performed a play for their parents.

senses.def: to do a task, action or piece of work
examples: The surgeon performed the operation in under two hours.

senses.def: to work or do something well or badly
examples: The new car performs well on snowy roads.
Students who sleep well tend to perform better in exams.

senses.def: the act of performing a play, concert or other entertainment
examples: The evening performance starts at 8 p.m.
Her performance in the film won her an Oscar.

senses.def: how well or badly a person, machine or company does something
examples: The company's performance improved in the second quarter.
His performance at work has been excellent.

senses.def: possibly; used when you are not certain
examples: Perhaps we should leave before the traffic gets bad.
It was perhaps the best meal I've ever had.

senses.def: used to make a request or suggestion more polite
examples: Perhaps you could call me back later?

note: A little more formal than maybe, which is more common in American conversation.

senses.def: a particular length of time, or a time in history
examples: The offer is valid for a limited period.
He lived in Paris during the postwar period.

senses.def: one of the parts of the school day when a subject is taught
examples: We have math in third period.

senses.def: (American) the mark (.) at the end of a sentence
examples: Don't forget to put a period at the end of the sentence.

senses.def: the time each month when a woman bleeds from her body
examples: She gets bad cramps during her period.

note: In speech, Americans say "period" at the end of a statement for emphasis: "I'm not going, period." British: full stop.

senses.def: lasting for a long time or forever; not expected to change
examples: She's looking for a permanent job, not just a summer position.
The injury caused permanent damage to his eyesight.

note: Opposite: temporary. "Permanent resident" = a person allowed to live in a country forever (green card holder in the US).

senses.def: in a way that lasts forever or for a very long time
examples: The factory closed permanently last year.
They moved permanently to Canada after retiring.

note: "For good" is a common informal equivalent: "They left for good."

senses.def: the act of allowing someone to do something, especially officially
examples: You need your parents' permission to go on the trip.
Nobody can enter the building without permission.

note: Uncountable: "get permission", not "get a permission". For a document, use permit.

senses.def: an official document that gives you the right to do something
examples: You need a permit to park on this street.
She applied for a work permit in Germany.

senses.def: (formal) to allow something or make it possible
examples: Smoking is not permitted anywhere in the building.
We'll have the party outside, weather permitting.

note: Stress: noun PERmit, verb perMIT /pərˈmɪt/. Doubles the t: permitted, permitting.

senses.def: to continue doing something even though it is difficult or others oppose it
examples: If the reporter persists in asking questions, call security.
She persisted with her studies despite many setbacks.

senses.def: to continue to exist
examples: If the pain persists, see a doctor.

senses.def: determined to keep doing something despite difficulties or opposition
examples: The salesman was very persistent and called me five times.
Her persistent efforts finally paid off.

senses.def: continuing for a long time or happening again and again
examples: He has had a persistent cough for weeks.
